meta.note: Real numbers measured on the flatwire dev machine and CI runners. Payload = 'records' shape, 50k elements (~12 MB) unless noted. See packages/*/bench/REPORT.md for full methodology.

encodeMemory.note: Peak/allocated memory to encode the whole collection vs streaming element-by-element. Lower is better.

decodeMemory.note: Peak live memory to decode-and-aggregate the whole collection vs streaming. Lower is better. Go/Java are GC-muddied in micro-benchmarks (see reports).

decodeTime.note: Median wall-clock time to decode-and-aggregate 50k records. flatwire trades CPU time for flat memory; the cost is small in native runtimes, large in pure-Python.

xml.note: Python: parsing a 12 MB XML document with ElementTree (DOM) vs flatwire streaming (iterparse). Streaming XML of large collections is a rare, real win.

msgpack.note: Python: bytes on the wire, JSON vs flatwire's streaming MessagePack (binary), wire-compatible with the reference msgpack library. Numeric-heavy payloads save more than this string-heavy shape.
